I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of.

Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does.

Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.

## Objective
- Build a browser card game from the user's one-line request: an online room-list duel with auto-created/auto-joined own room, 24 zones, life points that reach zero, and cards that are always visibly moving.
- Title chosen: **DUEL 24 // ZONE CARD ONLINE**.

## Requirements
- User's exact request: "起動時に必ず立てる自分のルームに必ず参加する状態のライフポイントをゼロにするカードゲームオンラインルームリストデュエル24ｿﾞｰﾝ必ずｶｰﾄﾞが動くDUEL"
- Interpreted as: auto-create and auto-join own room on startup, live online room list, LP reduced to 0 to win, 24-zone board, constant card animation.
- Must work as a static site with `index.html` at repo root (runtime serves static output).
- Mobile and desktop layouts required.

## Decisions
- Vanilla HTML/CSS/ES modules, no build step or packages.
- 24 zones total: 6 columns × 4 rows, 12 zones per player, lane-based attacks.
- LP 4000; energy starts at 3 and caps at 6; draw 1 per turn; 24-card deck.
- Cards have FLARE, PIERCE, DRAIN, LINK, AURA keywords.
- Summoning sickness enforced: units cannot attack the turn they are summoned.
- Lobby auto-creates room code `Z24-XXXX`, pins the player's room as joined, auto-invites an opponent after 8 seconds, and supports manual "招待".
- Opponent AI is local/simulated (no backend).
- Added room preview, 24-zone mini battlefield, and starter deck display to fill desktop lobby.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created full game UI: lobby, auto room creation/join, room list, 8 bots, invite flow, auto-match timer, duel screen, result overlay, rematch/lobby flows.
- Implemented rules engine, AI, combat, win condition, card animations, background canvas FX, WebAudio synth, sound toggle.
- Added 24-zone board, hand rendering, energy pips, LP bars, logs, inspector, responsive CSS, favicon.
- Verified lobby desktop/mobile, duel desktop/mobile render, summoning, AI turns, and unit attacks via Playwright.
- Fixed major bugs: defender row lookup, summoning sickness, room-list re-render blinking, mobile lobby clipping/grid height.

### Active
- Visual polish and final verification.
- Mobile duel screenshot shows board is oversized/empty on first turn and player HUD is cramped; hand cards extend beyond viewport with horizontal scroll.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Review `screenshots/duel-mobile.png` and tighten mobile duel spacing so board, HUDs, and hand fit better.
2. Verify direct LP attacks actually reduce AI LP (unit attacks were tested, but only a BREAK case; add a direct-attack UI test).
3. Fix inspector status text: currently shows `READY` for freshly summoned units; should show `SUMMONED`/`STANDBY` when `!duel.canAttack(unit)`.
4. Run a full game-to-result test through UI and capture `VICTORY`/`DEFEAT` overlay screenshot.
5. Test mobile select/summon/attack interactions and horizontal hand scrolling.
6. Take final desktop and mobile screenshots, check console/page errors and HTTP 4xx, then clean up server/browser processes.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: full lobby/duel markup and screen structure.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/styles.css`: all visual styling and responsive breakpoints.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/app.js`: lobby logic, `DuelGame` UI controller, AI sequencing, animations, interactions, `window.__duel24` test hooks.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/duel.js`: rules engine, combat math, AI planning, `canAttack`, `previewAttack`, `attack`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/cards.js`: 12 card definitions, factions, deck builder.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/audio.js`: WebAudio synth.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/fx.js`: canvas starfield and burst FX.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/assets/favicon.svg`: favicon.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: current lobby/duel screenshots including `duel-mobile.png`.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.

- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.

- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions })
const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } })
page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
const errors = []
const bad = []
page.on('pageerror', e => errors.push('PAGEERROR: ' + e.message))
page.on('console', m => { if (m.type() === 'error') errors.push('CONSOLE: ' + m.text()) })
page.on('response', r => { if (r.status() >= 400) bad.push(r.status() + ' ' + r.url()) })

await page.goto('http://localhost:3000', { waitUntil: 'load' })
await page.waitForTimeout(1800)
await page.screenshot({ path: 'screenshots/lobby-desktop.png', timeout: 60000 })
console.log('lobby', await page.evaluate(() => ({
  room: document.querySelector('#yourRoomCode')?.textContent?.trim(),
  joined: document.querySelector('.slot.you')?.innerText?.replace(/\n/g, ' '),
  rows: document.querySelectorAll('.room-row').length,
  scrollW: document.documentElement.scrollWidth,
  innerW: innerWidth,
})))

await page.click('#startBtn')
await page.waitForTimeout(3600)
const pick = await page.evaluate(() => {
  const d = window.__duel24.duel
  const i = d.hand.player.findIndex(c => c.cost <= d.energy.player)
  return i >= 0 ? { i, name: d.hand.player[i].name } : null
})
await page.locator('.hand-card').nth(pick.i).click({ force: true })
await page.waitForTimeout(200)
const zone = await page.evaluate(() => window.__duel24.duel.emptyZones('player')[0].id)
await page.locator(`.zone[data-zone="${zone}"]`).click({ force: true })
await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
await page.locator('#endTurnBtn').click({ force: true })
await page.waitForTimeout(2200)
await page.screenshot({ path: 'screenshots/duel-desktop.png', timeout: 60000 })
console.log('duel', await page.evaluate(() => ({
  state: window.__duel24.state(),
  scrollW: document.documentElement.scrollWidth,
  innerW: innerWidth,
  bodyH: document.body.scrollHeight,
  innerH: innerHeight,
  board: (() => { const r = document.querySelector('#board').getBoundingClientRect(); return { x: r.x, y: r.y, w: r.width, h: r.height } })(),
  hand: (() => { const r = document.querySelector('#hand').getBoundingClientRect(); return { x: r.x, y: r.y, w: r.width, h: r.height, scrollW: document.querySelector('#hand').scrollWidth } })(),
})))
console.log('errors', errors)
console.log('bad responses', bad)
await browser.close(); process.exit(0)
